result.title: GNN-Based Deep Reinforcement Learning for Coastal Emergency Response under Extreme Water Levels
result.comment: 6 pages, 1 figure, 1 table. Accepted at the Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning workshop at NeurIPS 2026. Code: https://github.com/marcellosano/coastal-emergency-drl
result.summary: When a storm surge approaches a coastal town, the emergency plan must be put into action quickly using water-level forecasts, flood extent, road access, vulnerable residents and shelters. Bringing this information together under time pressure is slow and depends on the duty officer's expertise. This paper is one step in a wider research line from data to safe decisions: machine learning to understand the hazard, reinforcement learning and planning to choose actions, large language models (LLMs) to explain and cross-check them, and an assurance layer that keeps people in charge. Here we address the action step on a real place. We ask whether a policy can learn the timing of emergency actions from decades of real events. Lido di Venezia is represented as a heterogeneous graph built from public elevation, road, building and census data and driven by hourly tide-gauge records from 1983 to 2024, with seven actions taken from the municipal emergency plan. A PPO policy is trained on this graph and compared, on storm windows unseen in training, with a rule-based system simulating the officer's discretionary decisions. On 18 historical test scenarios, PPO achieves a similar reduction in population exposure to the rule. With uncertain forecasts and limited protection it again performs similarly but does not outperform the tuned rule, and removing graph message passing does not substantially reduce performance. PPO therefore learns an effective protective response from an outcome-based reward alone: it is given the plan's actions and when each is allowed, but not the thresholds that tell the comparator when to act. Next steps test harder edge cases, move closer to a digital twin of the territory, and replace the simulated officer with assessment by emergency-management stakeholders, supported by LLM-based interpretation of each recommendation.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文把威尼斯利多岛建模为异构图（高程、道路、建筑、人口与1983–2024年潮位记录），用 PPO 学习市政应急预案七类行动的触发时机，并在18个历史情景上与规则系统对比：人口暴露降低幅度相近，去掉图消息传递后性能亦无明显下降。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「在不确定预报下何时触发行动」的时序决策与触发阈值，可能为 LVR 中何时停止/何时获取更多视觉证据的决策表述提供类比；消息传递消融未损性能这一现象也可供核查关系结构是否真被推理使用，但领域相距较远，需较多迁移判断。
